function: Joint learning of RIS mirror-unit orientation (yaw, roll), TDMA time fraction per user, and LED transmit power to maximize sum-rate, using soft actor-critic (p. 1-3).
system: Indoor visible-light downlink: one LED, K=5 single-PD users, reflecting mirror-array RIS with N units (up to 300), TDMA, 5x5x3 m room, B=200 MHz (p. 2, 4-5).
method: Soft actor-critic reinforcement learning on a constrained MDP; fully connected actor and two Q-networks, two hidden layers of 256 neurons, ReLU, Adam; trained by environment interaction (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Simulated Lambertian direct and specular RIS-reflected optical channel gains, 5x5x3 m room, K=5 users at random positions; no measured or standard dataset (p. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Policy trained by interaction with the same simulated room; results versus N up to 300 and noise power 1e-8 to 1e-5 W; no unseen scenario tested, retraining unstated (p. 5).
baselines: Non-learned: SCA [5]; SAC variants with random RIS orientation or without RIS [1]; learned: DDPG [6] on the same CMDP (p. 4).
metrics: Sum-rate (Mbps) versus number of RIS units; percentage sum-rate improvement over no-RIS; average reward versus training episodes (p. 5).
complexity: Order O(2K(5N+8)L1 + 3L1L2 + (4K(N+1)+2)L2) from the actor and critic layer dimensions of Table I; no runtime (p. 4).

N." is a sweep over the number of RIS units; p. 4: "Fig. 2(a) shows the convergence performance and the average reward of different schemes w.r.t. episodes of training"; missing: a policy trained in one room or N setting and tested in another, or a stated adaptation.
q3_support: p. 4: "3) DDPG-based algorithm in [6] for solving our formulated CMDP; 4) Sine-cosine algorithm (SCA) in [5] for solving our optimization problem in (6)"; p. 5: "average sum-rate gain of about 8.7% and 10.58% when comparing to the existing schemes of DDPG and SCA, respectively".
q4_support: p. 4: "the computational complexity of Algorithm 1 is" given as the order O(2K(5N+8)L1 + 3L1L2 + (4K(N+1)+2)L2), from the layer dimensions of Table I.

notes: Included as area 3: the learned SAC policy sets the RIS mirror orientation jointly with LED power and TDMA time fractions; RIS configuration is a physical-layer decision, so the joint decision passes the above-physical-layer check, and the RIS makes the single-LED, single-PD links admissible. q1 is 0: the Lambertian and specular-reflection channel is a custom simulator ([3], [8]); borderline only if the reviewer counts the Lambertian VLC model as widely shared. q2 is 0: sweeps over N and noise power, with retraining per setting unstated (the action size depends on N, Table I, p. 4). q3 rests on SCA [5] and DDPG [6].
